title: Cap. VIII Arg. 4 Resp.: will to punish follows foresight final perseverance — not cause of negative reprobation
pass_a_gloss: It is therefore true that God wills to show wrath and vengeance upon all the reprobated: but this will of inflicting vengeance is not immediately joined with that negative reprobation or non-election about which we dispute, but arises from the foresighted intervention of final perseverance in sin: which state of all the reprobate as infallibly future is foresighted by God as an event consequent upon negative reprobation, not as an antecedent cause. The argumentation is therefore little firm: God reprobating men wills also to punish the same, Therefore the cause of negative reprobation is foresighted sin.
pass_b_english: True: God wills to show wrath and vengeance on all the reprobate. But that will to inflict vengeance is not immediately joined to the negative reprobation or non-election we are disputing. It arises from foresighted intervention of final perseverance in sin — a state of all the reprobate foresighted by God as infallibly future as an event consequent on negative reprobation, not as an antecedent cause. So the argument is weak: God in reprobating also wills to punish them; therefore foresighted sin is the cause of negative reprobation.
source_text: Est igitur verum, Deum velle ostendere iram et vindictam in omnes reprobatos: sed haec voluntas vindictae inferendae cum reprobatione illa negativa sive non-electione, de qua disputamus, non est immediate conjuncta, sed exoritur ex praeviso interventu finalis perseverantiae in peccato: qui status omnium reproborum infallibiliter futurus praevidetur a Deo ut eventus consequens negativam reprobationem, non ut causa antecedens. Est igitur parum firma argumentatio, Deus reprobans homines, vult eosdem etiam punire, Ergo reprobationis negativae causa est peccatum praevisum.
